summary:
NOVAFOUNDERS is an interactive Mars exploration platform focused on the boxwork formations of lower Mount Sharp in Gale Crater. The project brings together Martian geological information, NASA orbital imagery, Curiosity rover observations, terrain elevation data and available environmental records in one platform.

Through the interactive Mars Explorer, users can investigate historical rover locations and geological features. The Terrain Analysis section helps explore elevation and slope characteristics, while the Science and Environment sections provide information about the geological context and recorded Martian conditions.

The platform also includes a Marswalk Planner that generates hypothetical exploration routes using terrain elevation and slope information, helping users compare possible paths between selected locations.

Our goal is to make Mars exploration data easier to understand and demonstrate how planetary science, geological analysis and digital mapping can support scientific investigation and future human exploration. The project also highlights data limitations and distinguishes actual observations from processed analysis and hypothetical route planning.
details:
NOVAFOUNDERS: Mars Boxwork Exploration Atlas

1. Project Overview

NOVAFOUNDERS is an interactive Mars exploration platform focused on the boxwork formations of lower Mount Sharp in Gale Crater, Mars.

Boxwork formations are interconnected networks of raised ridges and hollows that may preserve evidence of ancient groundwater activity. Our project explores these geological structures and investigates how orbital imagery, rover observations, terrain information and environmental records can help us understand the Martian surface.

Our study region includes several named locations investigated by NASA's Curiosity rover, including Altadena, Volcán Peña Blanca, Valle de la Luna and Nevado Sajama. These locations provide different geological perspectives on the boxwork region.

2. Important Locations in Our Study Region

Altadena – Initial Boxwork Investigation

Altadena was an early drill location during Curiosity's investigation of the boxwork unit. It provides a reference for studying the composition and geological characteristics of the rocks in the region.

Volcán Peña Blanca – Geological Context

This distinctive feature was investigated during Curiosity's regional exploration of the boxwork unit. It helps provide geological context between the initial investigation area and the more developed boxwork structures.

Valle de la Luna – Hollow Investigation

Valle de la Luna is a drill target located in a large topographic hollow called Monte Grande. Its rock sample provides an opportunity to investigate the material within the lower parts of the boxwork structures.

Nevado Sajama – Ridge Investigation

Nevado Sajama is a drill target on a boxwork ridge. Comparing its sample with the hollow sample from Valle de la Luna helps scientists investigate differences between ridge and hollow materials.

Together, these locations demonstrate why comparing different parts of the same geological formation is scientifically important.

3. What Does Our Project Do and How Does It Work?

Our website combines several exploration features into one interactive platform.

A. Mars Explorer – Location and Geological Exploration

The Mars Explorer presents the selected study region through an interactive map. Users can explore historical Curiosity rover locations, observation points and geological features.

The map helps users understand where important investigations took place, including the Altadena, Volcán Peña Blanca, Valle de la Luna and Nevado Sajama areas.

B. Terrain Analysis – Understanding the Martian Surface

This section presents elevation and slope information to help users understand the physical characteristics of lower Mount Sharp.

It helps examine:

  • Elevation differences across the study region.
  • Steep and gentle slopes.
  • Terrain variations between ridges and hollows.
  • Surface characteristics relevant to preliminary exploration planning.

C. Scientific and Geological Exploration – Understanding Boxwork

This section explains the geological significance of boxwork formations and the possible role of ancient groundwater.

The project explores the relationship between mineral deposition, fractures, erosion-resistant ridges and the hollows between them.

It also highlights why comparing the ridge target Nevado Sajama with the hollow target Valle de la Luna is scientifically valuable.

D. Environmental Information – Understanding Martian Conditions

The environmental section organises available historical observations, including temperature and atmospheric pressure records.

These observations provide additional context about the Martian environment. They are historical measurements rather than live weather information.

E. Marswalk Planner – Hypothetical Exploration Routes

The Marswalk Planner uses terrain elevation and slope information to generate and compare hypothetical routes between selected locations.

It demonstrates how surface characteristics can be considered when exploring possible paths across a region of Mars.

These routes are exploratory planning outputs, not certified astronaut navigation or safety recommendations.

4. Benefits of the Project

NOVAFOUNDERS provides several benefits:

  • Centralised exploration: Brings different categories of Mars information together in one platform.
  • Geological understanding: Helps users investigate boxwork formations and their possible formation history.
  • Location-based investigation: Connects scientific observations with named locations in the study region.
  • Terrain awareness: Makes elevation and slope information easier to explore.
  • Comparative science: Highlights the scientific value of comparing ridge and hollow samples.
  • Exploration planning: Demonstrates how terrain information can help compare hypothetical routes.
  • Educational accessibility: Makes planetary science more understandable through interactive mapping and visualisation.

5. Intended Impact

Our main aim is to demonstrate how different planetary science datasets can be brought together to investigate a specific region of Mars.

By connecting geological observations, terrain analysis and environmental information, the platform provides a more organised way to understand the Martian surface.

The project also demonstrates how scientific data could contribute to preliminary exploration planning and support the broader goal of future human exploration of Mars.

NOVAFOUNDERS is designed as an educational and research-support concept that encourages scientific investigation and data-driven thinking.

6. Tools, Technologies and Scientific Resources

Development tools and software:

  • Lovable – website development and interface creation.
  • Web-based mapping and data visualisation – presentation of geographical and scientific information.
  • ChatGPT – research assistance, understanding scientific concepts, organising project requirements and refining documentation.

NASA scientific resources:

  • HiRISE – high-resolution orbital imagery.
  • CTX – contextual imagery of the Martian surface.
  • MOLA – regional elevation information.
  • Mars Orbital Data Explorer – access to Mars mission datasets.
  • Curiosity rover observations – historical surface imagery and scientific investigations.
  • REMS – historical environmental observations, including atmospheric and temperature measurements.
  • CRISM – orbital mineralogical information for regional geological context.

These resources support our scientific research and the development of the platform. We distinguish between datasets directly displayed in the website and additional resources consulted for scientific context.

No specialised physical hardware was required to develop this web-based project.

7. Creativity and Innovation

The main creative idea behind NOVAFOUNDERS is to connect geological investigation with interactive mapping, terrain analysis and preliminary exploration planning.

Instead of presenting only a static map or separate scientific facts, our platform allows users to explore a specific geological region and understand how different types of observations contribute to its investigation.

The comparison between the ridge and hollow targets, particularly Nevado Sajama and Valle de la Luna, gives the project a focused scientific direction.

The Marswalk Planner adds another dimension by demonstrating how terrain information can be used in hypothetical exploration scenarios.

8. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered the following factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using credible scientific resources and distinguishing observations from interpretations.
  • Geographical focus: Concentrating on the boxwork region of lower Mount Sharp instead of attempting to cover the entire planet.
  • Location relevance: Including important Curiosity investigation areas to give the project a clear scientific focus.
  • Data resolution: Considering the differences between regional elevation datasets and higher-resolution local terrain information.
  • Data availability: Accounting for differences in coverage, observation dates and available measurements.
  • Terrain characteristics: Considering elevation and slope when comparing possible exploration routes.
  • Environmental limitations: Using historical observations rather than presenting them as live Martian conditions.
  • User accessibility: Organising scientific information into understandable sections.
  • Exploration relevance: Connecting geological research with the challenges of future human exploration.

9. Our Team's Vision

Through NOVAFOUNDERS, we aim to demonstrate how planetary science, digital mapping and creative problem-solving can work together to explore another world.

Our project brings attention to a scientifically interesting region of Mars and shows how different observations can help us investigate its geological history and surface characteristics.

We hope this platform encourages curiosity about Mars and demonstrates the importance of scientific data in preparing for future planetary exploration. https://gamma.app/docs/NOVAFOUNDERS-Mars-Boxwork-Exploration-Atlas-nczsjnrfv2we39n
